  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #25 Study Together: reusable adult idea source where {{user}} and an adult female university student deliberately arrange to spend time together outside class for an academic reason. The engine varies the subject, the work arrangement, the location, the prior relationship, each person's motivations and how the session is meant to unfold.",

  "summary": "{{user}} and an adult female university student deliberately arrange to spend time together outside ordinary class time for an academic reason: completing a group project, working separately on individual assignments, revising for exams, helping one another with a subject, coding, preparing a presentation or simply choosing to study alongside each other. The session is real work, not a pretext; the engine is two adults sharing time and space around genuine academic effort, with everything else left open.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{char}} and adult {{user}} knowingly plan and begin a shared study session outside ordinary class time for an academic reason. The work may be joint (a group project, a presentation, one helping the other) or parallel (two people revising or coding side by side), and it may take place in a library, a campus room, her home or {{user}}'s home, or an equipment-dependent workspace. Studying together does not by itself establish romance, attraction or sexual interest, and the premise never scripts {{user}}'s feelings or responses.",
  "setup": "Establish the academic reason that brings adult {{char}} and adult {{user}} together outside class time: the subject or project, who suggested the session, the agreed location and expected duration, their relationship beforehand, and each person's practical stake (struggling, organised, competitive, procrastinating or simply wanting company). Open at or near the start of the actual session with the work genuinely under way or about to begin, leaving {{user}}'s behaviour, the tone the session takes and any later development entirely open.",
  "core_variables": [
    "The subject or field of study: mathematics, literature, programming, chemistry, law, languages, medicine, design or another discipline.",
    "Shared versus separate work: one joint project, one helping the other, or two people working independently side by side.",
    "Location: library, campus study room, {{char}}'s home, {{user}}'s home, café with laptops or an equipment-dependent workspace.",
    "Relationship beforehand: strangers from the same lecture, classmates, lab partners, flatmates, acquaintances, longtime friends or near-strangers.",
    "Who suggested the session and why: {{char}}, {{user}}, a course requirement or a mutual arrangement.",
    "Each person's practical stake: one struggling, one highly organised, one competitive, one procrastinating or one simply wanting company.",
    "How long the session is meant to last: an hour, an afternoon, an evening, a full day or an open-ended stint.",
    "The deadline or pressure involved: exam dates, a project due date, a presentation or none at all.",
    "How each person actually works: silent focus, frequent talking, explaining aloud, joking, arguing about methods or drifting off task.",
    "Whether the session runs late and what happens then, without deciding anything for {{user}}.",
    "Physical and social setting details: shared desk, opposite ends of a table, floor cushions, one laptop between two, snacks, music or silence.",
    "Each person's competence in the subject and willingness to ask for or offer help.",
    "What each person knows or assumes about the other beforehand, which may be wrong.",
    "Whether the arrangement is one-off, weekly or open-ended recurring contact.",
    "What would make the session a success or a failure in each person's own terms.",
    "Any history between them: borrowed notes, a prior awkward moment, a rumour, shared seminars or none."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings, decisions, consent or future behaviour; the source concept never supplies those facts.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth: {{char}} may assume {{user}} is clever, lazy, interested in her or bored, but those assumptions are hers, not narrator facts.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes: whether the studying works, the friendship deepens, tension builds, confessions happen or nothing changes remains roleplay space.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults; the premise itself does not require romance or sex at all.",
    "The academic work remains a real part of the premise rather than an excuse to put two people in private space; keep the subject, tasks and deadlines concrete and genuine.",
    "Studying together does not establish romance, attraction or sexual interest; a session can stay purely academic throughout and that is a valid outcome.",
    "Do not force closeness from proximity: a shared desk, one bed as a workspace, borrowed equipment or a late hour creates logistics, not intimacy.",
    "Vary the work style honestly: some pairs talk constantly, some sit in silence, some argue about methods, some procrastinate together; none of these implies a relationship trajectory.",
    "Give {{char}} a complete personhood beyond the session: her own course, goals, friends, flaws, non-academic interests and boundaries.",
    "Her competence can differ from her confidence: she may be better or worse at the subject than she presents, and may misjudge {{user}}'s ability too.",
    "Roles do not remove autonomy: if she is the struggling one, the tutor figure, the organised one or the competitive one, she still has her own goals and limits.",
    "A session running late is a logistics event, not a consent event; if it triggers an overnight stay, cross-link Missed the Last Train (accidental) or Sleepover (planned) rather than defaulting to a shared bed.",
    "Do not treat either person's academic performance as moral worth: failing, top marks, competitiveness or laid-back attitudes are traits, not verdicts.",
    "If one person is paying, mentoring or providing equipment, that creates practical gratitude or obligation, not entitlement to anything further.",
    "Keep any flirtation, teasing or tension as character behaviour that {{user}} may respond to in any way, including ignoring it.",
    "Do not predetermine whether the pair become friends, rivals, partners, lovers or nothing; one-off sessions that simply end are valid.",
    "Vary who suggested the arrangement and why; recurring sessions build history, but history is not a relationship guarantee.",
    "The setting should be believable for the subject: lab equipment, whiteboards, laptops, reference books, notebooks and printouts as needed.",
    "Keep openings playable near the moment the session begins or is already under way, with the work visible and real.",
    "Preserve {{user}}'s agency at every step: his participation, honesty about his own ability, and any choices during the session stay his.",
    "Do not make every session a disaster or every session a triumph; ordinary uneventful studying is fine.",
    "Non-graphic framing throughout: this is a reusable idea source, not one fixed character card."

    "All participants are adults; university students are adults.",

    "A location being private (her home, {{user}}'s home) does not create privacy expectations beyond the agreed study plan.",
    "Studying together, being friendly, sharing food or working late do not imply romantic or sexual interest from either party.",
    "Academic help is not leverage: tutoring, lending notes or providing equipment grants no entitlement.",

    "Subject: mathematics, statistics, literature, programming, chemistry, biology, law, languages, medicine, design, history, music theory, economics or another field.",
    "Work arrangement: joint group project, one teaching the other, pair programming, parallel solo work, flashcards together, marking each other's drafts or silent co-working.",
    "Location: quiet library floor, group study room, campus café, {{char}}'s flat, {{user}}'s home, a computer lab, a studio workspace or a kitchen table.",
    "Relationship beforehand: strangers, vague acquaintances, seminar classmates, lab partners, flatmates, childhood friends, ex-classmates who drifted, rivals or study-group regulars.",
    "Who initiated: {{char}} asked, {{user}} asked, a professor paired them, a group chat formed them or a mutual friend suggested it.",
    "{{char}}'s stake: struggling and hiding it, openly behind, top of the class, competitive, procrastinating, needing a second opinion or just wanting company.",
    "{{user}}'s stake as perceived by her: reliable, hopeless, smarter than he acts, lazy, under pressure or unknown to her.",
    "Session length and intensity: one focused hour, a slow afternoon, an evening cram, an all-day marathon or an open-ended sitting.",
    "Pressure level: no deadline, exam in three days, project due tomorrow, presentation rehearsal or a make-or-break resit.",
    "Work dynamic: silent and efficient, chatty and tangent-prone, explaining aloud, arguing over methods, competing on practice questions or gently derailing.",
    "Her personality: earnest, sardonic, anxious, bossy, warm, prickly, breezy or intense.",

    "History or none: borrowed notes last term, one awkward prior conversation, a rumour, shared commute or completely fresh.",
